items.title: Announcing Example Lang 2.4
items.content:
The release team is happy to announce version 2.4 of Example Lang. This release stabilises async closures and improves incremental compile times by roughly 18% on the benchmark suite.

Upgrading is done with the usual toolchain command. Projects that pinned the 2.3 toolchain should check the compatibility notes, since two lints became errors by default.

Thanks to the 214 contributors who made this release possible, 61 of them for the first time.

items.title: Major cloud provider outage disrupts services across Europe
items.content:
A major cloud provider suffered a multi-hour outage on Wednesday morning that disrupted banking apps, airline check-in systems and several streaming services across Europe.

The company said a faulty configuration change to its load balancing layer was rolled out to three regions at once. Engineers began rolling it back at 06:40 UTC.

Customers reported elevated error rates for about four hours. The provider has promised a full incident report within a week.

items.title: Cloud outage: provider blames configuration change, Europe services restored
items.summary: Services hit by Wednesday's cloud outage in Europe have been restored, the provider said, blaming a configuration change. Some banks report a backlog of delayed payments.

items.title: Hands-on with the new e-ink laptop
items.summary: The first laptop with a colour e-ink main display is surprisingly usable for writing, but don't expect to watch video on it.

items.title: Telescope spots water vapour in atmosphere of temperate exoplanet
items.content:
Astronomers have detected water vapour in the atmosphere of an exoplanet that orbits within its star's habitable zone, according to a study published today.

The planet, roughly 1.6 times the radius of Earth, orbits a red dwarf 120 light-years away. The detection relied on 14 transits observed over two years.

The authors caution that water vapour alone is not evidence of habitability, and that stellar activity could partly mimic the signal.

Follow-up observations are scheduled for next spring.

items.title: A small open model for evidence-cited summarisation
items.content:
We are releasing a 3B-parameter model fine-tuned to produce summaries in which every sentence cites a span of the source document.

On our evaluation set, 94% of generated sentences were judged to be supported by their cited span, compared with 81% for a prompted baseline of the same size.

The model runs on a laptop CPU at around 20 tokens per second when quantised to four bits. Weights are available under an Apache 2.0 licence.

items.title: Inside the new borrow checker
items.content:
Over the last year the compiler team has been rewriting the borrow checker around a new formulation that accepts more correct programs.

The most visible change is that conditional returns of borrowed data now compile, a pattern that has been a common source of confusion.

This post walks through the design, the performance work needed to make it as fast as the old checker, and how it was tested against every public crate.

items.title: Why I'm taking a break from blogging
items.summary: After ten years of weekly posts, I'm stepping away for a while.

items.title: Deep-sea survey finds dozens of new species
items.content:
A six-week survey of a remote seamount chain has identified at least 40 animal species thought to be new to science.

The team used a remotely operated vehicle to collect samples at depths of up to 4,800 metres. Formal descriptions of the species will take several years.

items.title: Benchmarks are saturating; what should we measure next?
items.content:
Several widely used reasoning benchmarks now show scores above 95% for the strongest models, which makes them poor at telling systems apart.

We argue for evaluations built around long tasks with verifiable outcomes, and describe three we are publishing today.

Update: we corrected the score reported for one baseline after a reader spotted a grading error.

items.title: European banks report payment delays after cloud outage
items.content:
Several European banks said customer payments were delayed by up to six hours after Wednesday's cloud outage, and that backlogs should clear by the evening.

Regulators said they had asked the cloud provider for details of the configuration change and its testing process.

items.title: Chipmaker shares rise on strong forecast
Critical flaw in popular VPN appliance exploited in the wild
items.content:
A critical authentication bypass in a widely deployed VPN appliance is being actively exploited, the vendor confirmed on Wednesday, urging customers to patch immediately.

The flaw, tracked as CVE-2026-41120, lets an unauthenticated attacker reach the management interface. Researchers counted more than 9,000 devices exposed to the internet.

Fixed firmware is available for all supported versions, and the vendor has published indicators of compromise for incident responders.

items.title: VPN appliance zero day: what we know so far
items.summary: Attackers began exploiting the VPN appliance flaw at least four days before a patch was available, according to incident responders. Exposed management interfaces are the main risk.

items.title: Browser update fixes two zero-day vulnerabilities
items.content:
A browser update released overnight fixes two vulnerabilities that were already being exploited, one in the JavaScript engine and one in the graphics stack.

Users should restart their browser to apply the update. Enterprise administrators can force the update through policy.

items.title: Phishing kit abuses calendar invites to bypass email filters
items.content:
A phishing kit sold on criminal forums sends fake meeting invitations that place malicious links directly in the recipient's calendar, avoiding many email filters.

Security teams can reduce the risk by disabling automatic calendar entries from external senders.

items.title: Reusable booster completes its 30th flight
items.content:
A first-stage booster landed after its 30th flight on Wednesday, extending the record for reuse of an orbital rocket stage.

The company says inspection between flights now takes under a week, down from several months for early boosters.

items.title: Lunar lander enters orbit ahead of south pole touchdown
items.content:
A robotic lander entered lunar orbit early on Thursday after a five-day cruise, setting up an attempt to land near the Moon's south pole.

Controllers will lower the orbit over the next two days. The landing site was chosen for its likely water ice in permanently shadowed craters.

If successful, the lander will operate for about 14 Earth days until lunar night.

items.title: Moon lander reaches lunar orbit; south pole landing set for Saturday
items.summary: The lander is now circling the Moon and is scheduled to attempt its south pole landing on Saturday.

items.title: Astronauts finish seven-hour spacewalk to replace solar array
items.content:
Two astronauts completed a seven-hour spacewalk to install a new roll-out solar array on the space station.

The array will restore power lost as older panels degraded.

items.title: Grid batteries supplied a record share of evening peak demand
items.content:
Batteries supplied 31% of evening peak electricity demand on the regional grid on Tuesday, a record, as solar output stored during the day was released after sunset.

Operators say battery capacity has tripled in two years, reducing the need for gas plants that run only at peak times.

items.title: October heatwave breaks records across southern Europe
items.content:
Temperatures above 35°C were recorded in parts of Spain, Portugal and Italy this week, breaking October records at more than 40 weather stations.

Climate scientists say heatwaves this late in the year have become several times more likely because of global warming.

Authorities issued water restrictions in two regions already affected by drought.

items.title: Offshore wind auction draws fewer bids as costs rise
items.content: The latest offshore wind auction attracted bids for only half of the available capacity, as developers cited higher costs for turbines and financing.

items.title: Landfill methane leaks underestimated, satellite study finds
items.content:
Satellite measurements suggest methane emissions from large landfills are on average 40% higher than reported in national inventories.

Because methane traps far more heat than carbon dioxide over two decades, the authors say capturing landfill gas is one of the cheapest climate measures available.

items.title: Chipmaker shares jump 12% as data-center revenue beats forecasts
items.content:
Shares of the chipmaker rose 12% in early trading after it reported data-center revenue well above analysts' forecasts and raised its outlook for the year.

Demand for AI accelerators continues to outstrip supply, the company said, though it expects growth to slow next year.

items.title: Climate-tech startup raises $40M to build sodium-ion batteries
items.content:
A two-year-old startup has raised $40 million to build sodium-ion batteries for grid storage, which avoid lithium and cobalt.

The company plans a pilot factory next year and says its cells cost 30% less than comparable lithium iron phosphate cells.

items.title: Central bank holds rates, signals a cut in December
items.content:
The central bank kept its main interest rate unchanged on Wednesday but said a cut in December was likely if inflation keeps slowing.

Markets moved to price in a quarter-point cut, and bond yields fell.

items.title: Developer tools startup acquired for $1.2 billion
items.content: A large software company agreed to buy a developer tools startup for $1.2 billion, its biggest acquisition in three years.

items.title: Notes from a week without a smartphone
items.content:
For one week I left my phone in a drawer and carried a notebook and a paper map instead.

The hardest part was not navigation but two-factor authentication, which assumes everyone has a phone at hand at all times.

items.title: What I learned rebuilding my homelab
items.content:
I replaced three old machines with one low-power mini PC and moved everything into containers.

Power use dropped from 90 W to 14 W, and backups finally run every night.

items.title: Example Lang 2.4.1 point release fixes a regression
items.content: Version 2.4.1 fixes a regression in 2.4 that caused incorrect warnings for some async closures. Upgrading is recommended for all users of 2.4.

items.title: Agents that check their own work: a practical guide
items.content:
Language-model agents make fewer mistakes when they verify intermediate results with tools, such as running tests or re-reading a source, before continuing.

This guide shows three verification patterns and measures how much each one reduces errors on long coding tasks.

items.title: Bird migration timing shifts with warmer autumns
items.content:
Analysis of 50 years of bird-ringing records shows several songbird species now leave for the winter up to two weeks later than in the 1970s.

The shift tracks rising autumn temperatures, but researchers worry it may leave birds out of step with food supplies along their routes.

items.title: Smartwatch maker recalls 200,000 devices over battery swelling
items.content: A smartwatch maker is recalling about 200,000 devices after reports that batteries could swell and crack the case. No injuries have been reported.
